claims.claim: Mandating low-emission hydrogen in existing applications such as steel raises supply costs passed on to consumers, but the effect on final product prices (e.g. a car) is expected to be only marginal.
claims.activity: use of low-emission hydrogen in steel production under quotas or mandates
claims.policy_lever: regulatory measures such as quotas or mandates that enforce the use of low-emission hydrogen

evidence.quote: this would result in higher supply costs that will be passed on to consumers, but the impact on the final products is expected to be rather limited: for example, the cost of a car would increase only marginally when produced with steel produced using low -emission hydrogen.
adopting regulatory measures such as quotas or mandates that enforce the use of low -emission hydrogen in existing applications

claims.claim: Adopting low-emission hydrogen is the only decarbonisation option for refining, ammonia production and methanol production, so enforcing its use in these sectors would decarbonise them.
claims.activity: use of low-emission hydrogen in refining, ammonia and methanol production
claims.policy_lever: combining support measures with regulatory frameworks to enforce the adoption of low-emission hydrogen

evidence.quote: enforce the adoption of low -emission hydrogen in sectors where it is the only decarbonisation alternative: refining, ammonia production and methanol production
combining support measures with regulatory frameworks to enforce the adoption of low -emission hydrogen

claims.claim: Multilateral development banks' growing hydrogen finance, mostly loans to EMDE governments, mobilises resources for developing countries that can fund feasibility studies, capacity building and support to project developers.
claims.activity: multilateral development bank financing of hydrogen projects in EMDEs

evidence.quote: Nine-tenths of the funds have been made available as loans to governments of EMDEs. This money can be used for project feasibility studies, capacity building and support to project developers.
Multilateral development banks stepped up their financial commitments in the area of hydrogen in 2022 and so far this has continued apace in 2023
the European Investment Bank (EIB) and World Bank have made the largest commitments, notably to India, Brazil and Chile

claims.claim: Multilateral finance for hydrogen supports implementation of hydrogen strategies in countries with fewer resources, with funds directed to prospective hydrogen exporters such as Brazil, Namibia and India.
claims.activity: multilateral development bank financing of hydrogen in prospective exporting countries

evidence.quote: Multilateral finance can assist the implementation of hydrogen strategies in countries that have fewer resources to invest in this area. In particular, some of the finance has been directed to countries that are exploring opportunities to export hydrogen.

the EIB has committed around USD 1 billion from EU countries – some of which could become hydrogen importers – to Brazil, and over USD 0.5 billion to Namibia. It has also committed more than USD 1 billion to India.

claims.claim: Japan's hydrogen import strategy could create synergies in international energy trading and business cooperation that drive development and make hydrogen technologies more affordable.
claims.activity: Japan's national hydrogen strategy based on international hydrogen imports and partnerships

evidence.quote: Japan’s strategy could have a positive global impact and contribute to the creation of new synergies regarding international energy trading and business cooperation. These will be crucial in driving development and making technologies more affordable.

claims.claim: Early alkaline electrolysers used asbestos gas separators, which can pose large health hazards; asbestos was later replaced by other separator materials.
claims.activity: use of asbestos diaphragms in alkaline electrolysers
claims.policy_lever: replacing asbestos with other separator materials such as ZIRFON or composite zirconium oxide

evidence.quote: Asbestos can pose large health hazards, but this was not known until late in the 20th century
asbestos started to be replaced by other materials (such as ZIRFON®)

claims.claim: Reducing the diaphragm thickness of alkaline electrolysers improves efficiency and reduces electricity consumption, e.g. from 53% to 75% efficiency when thinning from 460 to 50 micrometres.
claims.condition: diaphragm thickness reduced from about 460 µm to 50 µm

evidence.quote: Reducing diaphragm thickness: This could improve efficiency and reduce electricity consumption.
Decreasing this to 50 µm would contribute to improving the efficiency from 53% to 75% at 1 A/cm2

claims.claim: Thinner electrolyser diaphragms increase gas permeation, which raises safety concerns at the plant.

evidence.quote: this comes at a cost of higher gas permeation, which contributes to higher safety concerns

claims.claim: Using green hydrogen in hard-to-abate sectors reduces their GHG emissions, which requires large volumes (400 Mt by 2050 from 5 TW of electrolysers in IRENA's roadmap).
claims.activity: use of green hydrogen in hard-to-abate sectors
claims.condition: rapid scale-up of electrolyser capacity to produce large amounts of green hydrogen

evidence.quote: Reducing GHG emissions in hard-to-abate sectors through the use of green hydrogen will require large amounts of it, larger than current (mostly grey) hydrogen production.
That, in turn, requires a rapid scale-up in the number and overall capacity of the electrolysers used to make hydrogen.
foresees 400  Mt of green hydrogen consumed by 2050, produced by a total installed capacity of electrolysers of 5 TW

claims.claim: Electrolyser deployment can divert renewable electricity away from end uses that would cut GHG emissions more effectively; electrolyser capacity targets can avoid this by ensuring renewables and electrolysers are developed in parallel.
claims.activity: electrolyser capacity deployment for hydrogen production
claims.condition: if renewable and electrolyser capacity are not developed in parallel
claims.policy_lever: electrolyser capacity targets in national hydrogen strategies

evidence.quote: avoiding the diversion of renewable energy from end uses that may be more effective in decreasing GHG emissions
Target setting can ensure the appropriate parallel development of renewable energy and electrolyser capacities
